title: Claims Manual, Harbison Protection Contracts: Filing a Claim and the Coverage Tests
content:
### 1. Opening a claim

A claim on a Harbison Protection Contracts contract is opened by the agent for each failed component a Harbison technician diagnosed and repaired on a service call. Repairs by any other contractor are never reimbursed on a tier that does not reimburse third-party repairs. A claim is filed only against a contract whose status is active, as the contract record shows.

The failure date is the completed date of that service call, and the original decision is made on the filing date.

### 2. Filing deadline

A claim is accepted for decision only when it is filed no later than the tier's claim filing deadline, in calendar days, after the failure was diagnosed. Filing-deadline days are counted as calendar days with the service call's completed date as day 0, and a claim filed on the last day is accepted. The completed date is read from the service call record.

### 3. Order of the coverage tests

The claim is decided in the following order, and the first failing test governs the denial reason:

| Order | Test | Denial reason when it fails |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | the failure date falls within the coverage start through the coverage end | outside the coverage term |
| 2 | the component is in the tier's covered components | component not covered |
| 3 | the claim was filed within the deadline | filed after the deadline |
| 4 | where the tier requires maintenance, documented maintenance is current | maintenance not documented |
| 5 | the failure does not stem from an excluded cause: flood, fire, lightning or power surge, freezing of an unheated space, rodent or pest damage, or repair or alteration by anyone other than Harbison | excluded cause |
| 6 | the contract's remaining claim benefit is above $0.00 | limit exhausted |

### 4. Documented maintenance

Maintenance is current only when the most recent documented maintenance on the failed unit was completed no more than the tier's maintenance interval in months plus its grace days before the failure date. When the coverage start is itself later than that same cut-off, no maintenance record is required. Documented maintenance is one of the tier's accepted records: a completed Comfort Club tune-up on that unit, or a paid precision tune-up service call on that unit. A customer's own receipt from another contractor is not accepted. The test reads the unit's Comfort Club visit entries and its service calls and their tune-up charge lines.

Boundary cases (hypothetical, stated against the cut-off, which lies the interval plus the grace days before the failure date):

- maintenance completed on the cut-off day: current;
- maintenance completed the day before the cut-off: not current, unless the coverage start is later than the cut-off;
- coverage start the day after the cut-off and no maintenance on record: no maintenance record is required.

### 5. Parts and the manufacturer

Parts are paid only for components the tier covers within its parts coverage years, and only when no manufacturer parts warranty applies on the failure date, because parts are secondary to the manufacturer on every tier. The manufacturer term is the registered parts years confirmed by the installation's manufacturer registration entry, or, when no registration exists, the manufacturer's unregistered parts term set for the installation under Replacement System Installations, counted from the installed date.

The former clause — "When the manufacturer warranty supplies the part, the claim is partially approved for the parts with the manufacturer's parts coverage as the reason and pays the remaining covered components; otherwise a claim passing every test is approved" — is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current decision basis of each tier.

### 6. Labor

Labor is paid only within the tier's labor coverage years, which are the contract term.
